stories.headline: DeepSeek open-sources TileLang and kernel libraries for Huawei's Ascend chips, a CUDA alternative

key_facts.fact: On Wednesday, September 30, 2026, DeepSeek said on its official WeChat account that it has partnered with Huawei to develop programming tools for Huawei's Ascend chips and is open-sourcing infrastructure for the Ascend platform, including the high-level programming language TileLang plus compute and communication libraries.
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese AI firm DeepSeek said on Wednesday it has partnered with Huawei Technologies to develop programming tools for Huawei's Ascend chips... it was open-sourcing infrastructure for Huawei's Ascend platform, including a high-level programming language called TileLang, along with related compute and communication libraries.

key_facts.fact: DeepSeek said TileLang offers 'a simpler programming model' than Nvidia's CUDA, and that the first priority for an 'independent, self-controlled GPU software ecosystem' is a universal, easy-to-program high-level language that can still reach the hardware's full performance.
key_facts.excerpt: "TileLang was created precisely to meet this need," the company said, adding that it offers "a simpler programming model" than Nvidia's CUDA, improving development efficiency and simplifying code logic.

key_facts.fact: DeepSeek released six software modules that mirror its earlier open-source tools for Nvidia chips; TileLang now officially supports Huawei's Ascend 950 accelerators with native code generation, automatic scheduling and synchronisation.
key_facts.excerpt: Hangzhou-based DeepSeek released six software modules that mirror its prior open-source tools for Nvidia's AI chips... it now officially supports Huawei's Ascend 950 accelerators, offering "native code generation, automatic scheduling, and synchronisation"

key_facts.fact: The six projects are TileLang, DeepGEMM-Ascend, DeepEP-Ascend, TileKernels, FlashMLA and DeepSelect; DeepGEMM-Ascend and DeepEP-Ascend are new Ascend-specific repos with APIs matching the Nvidia versions, and the two companies are jointly advancing a 128-card Ascend 950 supernode.
key_facts.excerpt: 本次开源共涉及 TileLang、DeepGEMM-Ascend、DeepEP-Ascend、TileKernels、FlashMLA、DeepSelect 六个 GitHub 项目... 双方已共同推进基于昇腾 950 的 128 卡超节点方案。

key_facts.fact: DeepSeek said it worked with Huawei on the Ascend 950 chips and credited Huawei with 'unwavering and strong support' during R&D.
key_facts.excerpt: DeepSeek stated it worked with Huawei on its Ascend 950 chips and praised the vendor for providing "unwavering and strong support" during R&D.

stories.headline: NYT: Meta claims research tax credits by labeling its AI data centers 'experimental'

key_facts.fact: The New York Times reported that Meta classifies its AI data centers as experimental 'pilot models' so that Nvidia chips bought for them qualify for a 1980s-era federal research and experimentation tax credit; the distinction between chips for AI and ordinary data centers began in late 2024.
key_facts.excerpt: Starting in late 2024, the company drew a tax distinction between chips destined for AI data centers and those going to ordinary data centers... By treating the facilities as "pilot models" under a tax credit created in the 1980s, Meta has been claiming that expensive Nvidia chips qualify

key_facts.fact: Meta's savings from the research tax credit rose from $700 million in 2023 to $2 billion in 2024 and $3.9 billion in 2025, making it the largest beneficiary of the credit among publicly traded companies.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta's savings from the research tax credit rose from $700 million in 2023 to $2 billion in 2024 and then $3.9 billion in 2025, according to the Times. That makes Meta the largest beneficiary of the research tax credit among publicly traded companies

key_facts.fact: Per the NYT, Meta told the IRS its AI data centers were a 'giant experiment that could fail,' citing four people familiar with the company's operations.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta told the Internal Revenue Service that its AI data centers were a "giant experiment that could fail," the newspaper reported, citing four people familiar with the company's operations.

key_facts.fact: Meta's reserve against potential IRS challenges rose 45%, from $12.9 billion to $18.74 billion, and its filings cite 'uncertainties with our research tax credits' as the main driver of that exposure.
key_facts.excerpt: Over that same span, the reserve Meta holds against potential IRS challenges climbed 45% — from $12.9 billion to $18.74 billion.

key_facts.fact: Meta spokesman Andy Stone said the company uses 'the tax incentives Congress established decades ago'; Meta said it invested $200 billion in research over five years, including $57 billion last year.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta defended the practice, saying it invested $200 billion in research over five years, including $57 billion last year. "Like other companies that invest at this scale, we use the tax incentives Congress established decades ago to encourage this type of domestic investment,"

key_facts.fact: Tax expert Andre Shevchuck of BPM called describing data centers as experimental facilities 'kind of wild and out there'; the research credit is estimated to cost $32.1 billion in 2025, and Meta's credits alone are over 10% of that.
key_facts.excerpt: Andre Shevchuck, a partner at advisory firm BPM... told the Times that describing data centers as experimental facilities is "kind of wild and out there."... will reduce government revenues by $32.1 billion in 2025. Meta's credits by themselves represent over ten percent of that total cost

stories.headline: GPU cloud GMI Cloud raises $668M in Nvidia-backed equity and a CTBC-led credit line

key_facts.fact: GMI Cloud closed $668 million of financing on September 30, 2026: $223 million in equity led by ARCHIV with Nvidia participating, plus $445 million in credit led by Taiwan's CTBC, per The Information.
key_facts.excerpt: GMI Cloud closed $668M on Sept 30: $223M equity led by ARCHIV with Nvidia participating, plus $445M credit led by Taiwan's CTBC.

key_facts.fact: The equity is a Series B; other participants include Redwood, DSC Investment, KT Corp., Kyobo Life, KB Investment and Trend Micro. SiliconANGLE put the ChinaTrust credit facility at $440 million.
key_facts.excerpt: closed on a $223 million Series B round of funding led by the robotics and AI-focused investment firm ARCHIV, with participation from Nvidia Corp., Redwood, DSC Investment, KT Corp., Kyobo Life, KB Investment and Trend Micro Inc. At the same time, it has secured a $440 million credit facility from ChinaTrust Commercial Bank

key_facts.fact: The CTBC facility is described as APAC's first GPU-backed syndicated loan; debt is capped at 55% of the value of Nvidia's master service agreements, with collateral in a 16MW Taiwan AI Factory designed for 7,488 Nvidia GPUs and about $546 million of server capex.
key_facts.excerpt: APAC's first GPU-backed syndicated loan, with total debt capped at 55% of the value of Nvidia's master service agreements... a 16MW build in Taiwan, the Taiwan AI Factory, slated to house 7,488 Nvidia GPUs with total server capex of about US$546 million.

key_facts.fact: A loan banker told IFR that Nvidia, which both uses and leases capacity and takes a revenue share, sits in a 'quasi-super-senior position' ahead of bank fees, interest and principal.
key_facts.excerpt: "In payment waterfall terms, Nvidia is effectively in a quasi-super-senior position for its shareable revenue, ahead of bank fees, interest and principal," a Hong Kong-based loan banker told IFR.

key_facts.fact: GMI Cloud's contracted annual recurring revenue has surpassed $600 million, and the money will expand GPU capacity across the US and Asia.
key_facts.excerpt: Contracted annual recurring revenue has surpassed $600 million... GMI Cloud has assembled $668 million in financing to expand its artificial intelligence infrastructure across the United States and Asia

stories.headline: PaleBlueDot AI seeks $600M private credit to buy chips in Korea for China's Xiaohongshu

key_facts.fact: US-based PaleBlueDot AI is in talks with lenders including Brookfield Asset Management for $600 million of private credit to buy chips for its site in South Korea, Bloomberg reported on September 30, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: US-based PaleBlueDot AI is in talks with potential lenders including Brookfield Asset Management for $600 million of private credit to buy chips for its site in South Korea

key_facts.fact: The chips would be used by Xiaohongshu (RedNote), the Chinese lifestyle social media platform; Brookfield is set to provide part of the loan, which would yield in the low teens.
key_facts.excerpt: The chips would be used by Xiaohongshu, the popular Chinese lifestyle social media platform also known as RedNote... Brookfield is set to provide part of the loan, which would pay a yield in the low teens

key_facts.fact: The terms are not final; the deal would be more than double the $255 million GPU-backed note PaleBlueDot closed with Brookfield and Tor Investment Management in July 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Terms are not final... The deal would more than double the $255 million GPU-backed note PaleBlueDot closed with Brookfield and Tor Investment Management in July 2026.

key_facts.fact: Palo Alto-based PaleBlueDot, founded last year, closed a $150 million Series B in January 2026 at a valuation above $1 billion and operates in Japan, South Korea and Singapore.
key_facts.excerpt: The company closed a $150 million Series B round in January 2026, pushing its valuation above $1 billion... PaleBlueDot's operational footprint already spans multiple Asian markets, including Japan, South Korea, and Singapore.

stories.headline: Netlist asks US trade tribunal to ban imports of Micron HBM used in Nvidia, Google, Broadcom gear

key_facts.fact: On Tuesday, September 29, 2026, Netlist said it had filed a new complaint at the US International Trade Commission (first filed under seal on Friday) seeking to block imports of Micron memory chips used in Google, Nvidia and Broadcom AI products.
key_facts.excerpt: Computer-memory company Netlist said on Tuesday that it has filed a new complaint at a U.S. trade tribunal seeking to block imports of Micron memory chips used in Google, Nvidia and Broadcom products for AI computing.

key_facts.fact: Netlist alleges Micron's chips and the tech giants' products infringe two of its patents covering high-bandwidth memory (HBM), and asks for an import bar on Micron DRAM plus Google, Nvidia and Broadcom GPUs, servers and other products using it.
key_facts.excerpt: Micron's chips and the tech giants' products infringe two of its patents covering "high bandwidth memory" technology. The company asked the tribunal to bar imports of Micron dynamic random access memory (DRAM) devices and Google, Nvidia and Broadcom graphics processing units, servers and other products

key_facts.fact: Netlist won a $445 million patent verdict against Micron in Marshall, Texas in 2024, filed another ITC complaint against Micron in August over chips in Super Micro, HPE and Lenovo products, and settled with Samsung in August after $421 million in verdicts.
key_facts.excerpt: Netlist won a $445 million patent infringement verdict against Micron in Marshall, Texas federal court in 2024. Netlist filed another ITC complaint against Micron in August over memory chips used in Super Micro Computer, Hewlett Packard Enterprise and Lenovo products. Netlist settled a separate memory-patent dispute with Samsung in August after winning $421 million

key_facts.fact: Netlist CEO CK Hong said the action protects technologies 'now used in rapidly expanding AI infrastructure'; Micron, Google, Nvidia and Broadcom did not immediately comment.
key_facts.excerpt: "Netlist has spent decades developing advanced memory technologies now used in rapidly expanding AI infrastructure," Netlist CEO CK Hong said in a statement.

key_facts.fact: DigiTimes reports the proceedings target Micron and downstream customers Nvidia, Broadcom and Google over alleged unauthorized use of Netlist's patented HBM technology.
key_facts.excerpt: Netlist has begun legal proceedings against Micron and downstream customers Nvidia, Broadcom, and Google to stop them from allegedly using the company's patented high-bandwidth memory (HBM) technology without authorization

stories.headline: Chip startup Efficient Computer raises ~$100M at a $650M valuation for dataflow processors

key_facts.fact: Efficient Computer, a Carnegie Mellon spinout based in Pittsburgh, said on Tuesday, September 29, 2026, that it raised $100 million at a $650 million valuation, bringing total funding to $176 million.
key_facts.excerpt: Efficient Computer, a chip startup spun out of Carnegie Mellon University, on Tuesday said it has raised $100 million in additional funding, bringing its valuation to $650 million... Efficient has raised $176 million to date.

key_facts.fact: The Series B of more than $97 million was led by TQ Ventures, with Eclipse, Union Square Ventures, Toyota Ventures and others, seven months after a $60 million Series A.
key_facts.excerpt: TQ Ventures leads a Series B of more than $97M for Efficient Computer at a $650M valuation... Total funding reaches $173M, seven months after a $60M Series A led by Triatomic Capital.

key_facts.fact: Efficient builds dataflow-architecture chips it says are 10 to 100 times more energy-efficient than Intel or Nvidia architectures; its first chips ship for drones and small robots, with data-center chips planned later.
key_facts.excerpt: Efficient is developing chips with what is known as data flow architectures that can be both faster and 10 to 100 times more energy-efficient than the architectures used by Intel Corp or Nvidia Corp... the first chips that is shipping are aimed at drones and small robots.

key_facts.fact: Its Electron E1 processor is in volume production, but the company has not disclosed revenue or unit shipments.
key_facts.excerpt: Its Electron E1 chip is in volume production, but the company has not disclosed revenue.

stories.headline: CScale exits stealth with $145M, backed by Nvidia and Intel Capital, for optical AI interconnect

key_facts.fact: CScale exited stealth on September 30, 2026, announcing a $145 million Series C to develop optical interconnect for AI scale-up, bringing total funding to $188 million.
key_facts.excerpt: CScale today exited stealth, announcing $145 million in Series C funding to accelerate development and commercialization of optical interconnect for AI scale-up... The round brings the company's total funding to $188 million.

key_facts.fact: The round was co-led by Atreides Management, Valor Equity Partners and Premji Invest; NVIDIA and Intel Capital joined as CScale's first strategic investors.
key_facts.excerpt: The round was co-led by Atreides Management, Valor Equity Partners, and Premji Invest. Sutter Hill Ventures... continued its support alongside existing investor Maverick Silicon. NVIDIA and Intel Capital joined as CScale's first strategic investors.

key_facts.fact: The Palo Alto startup is building optical links designed to keep AI clusters running when lasers fail, containing failures instead of interrupting computation.
key_facts.excerpt: It is building optical links meant to keep AI clusters running when lasers fail.

key_facts.fact: Founded in 2023, CScale is led by CEO Martin Lund, a veteran of Cisco, Microsoft, Cadence, Broadcom and Intel, and has about 85 employees.
key_facts.excerpt: It was founded in 2023 and is led by CEO Martin Lund, who brings three decades of silicon and network engineering leadership from Cisco, Microsoft, Cadence, Broadcom, and Intel... CScale has approximately 85 employees globally.
